locations.description: Access paths to the same content; the first is canonical. An absolute URL, or a path relative to the record file for a small metadata file committed beside it (README, agent guide, code list, thumbnail).

name.description: Asset name; must be unique across data[] and additional_assets[].

roles.description: Asset roles. Suggested values, not a closed set: `metadata`, `validation`, `describedby` (human documentation such as a README), `agents` (a Markdown guide for AI agents: keys and join columns, quirks, CRS consequences, tested queries), `thumbnail`, `overview`, `visual`, `example` (a code file: a runnable usage example, e.g. a notebook or SQL file).

orcid.description: ORCID iD of the named person.

examples: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA)
International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT)
International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT)

roles.description: Roles this contact holds (vocab/contact_role.json). At least one contact of a record should be the licensor.

description.description: What this entry holds and how it differs from the record's other entries: which part of the dataset it covers (one table, region, or period), or which layout of the same data it is (e.g. time- vs space-optimized chunks) and when to use it.

checksum.description: Digest of the single file this entry names, as <algorithm>:<hex>. Not for templated or indexed entries; a cdh-inventory carries per-file checksums.

name.description: Asset name; must be unique across data[] and additional_assets[].

structures.description: Names of the structures[] this asset holds. Required when the record has more than one structure; omitted, the asset holds the record's only structure. Structure membership must be verified before publication.

href_template.description: Optional relative file-name pattern appended to each locations[].url. Each {token} must match a dimensions[].name or be the reserved {variable} token, which expands over variables[].name; the entry expands to one item per combination of the tokens' values. A token on a type: temporal dimension may carry a strftime format ({date:%Y.%m.%d}, directives %Y %m %d only) when the file name spells the date differently from the ISO value. When absent, locations[].url are full file URLs and the entry is a single asset.

file_index.description: Indexes that list or open this entry's files as one dataset, per the File indexes section of standard.md. Each entry is one index file, or with href_template one per rendered path; its locations[] are the same file at several addresses. format names the specification the file follows. CDH does not open index files. Mutually exclusive with href_template on the entry.

format.description: Specification the index file follows: stac-geoparquet (STAC Items as GeoParquet), gti (GDAL Tile Index), vrt (GDAL Virtual Raster), kerchunk (kerchunk reference file), icechunk (Icechunk repository with virtual chunks), or cdh-inventory (CDH CSV file list of absolute URLs).

locations.description: Copies of the index file; the first is canonical. Absolute URLs; a cdh-inventory may instead use a path relative to the record file when committed beside it.

title.description: Optional label, e.g. which scheme the index's internal paths use.

media_type.description: IANA media type of the index file itself, when it has one. Optional; useful for gti (GeoPackage, FlatGeobuf, or Parquet).

href_template.description: Optional pattern appended to each locations[].url when there is one index file per slice, e.g. one VRT per map. Same tokens and rules as the entry-level href_template; together the rendered files are one complete index.

spatial.description: Coverage of this asset alone, for selecting files by area. Same shapes as the top-level spatial. Omit when unknown; the top-level bbox is not copied down.

bbox.description: Spatial extent. A single bounding box, or a list of boxes for disjoint coverage - each box is a real area covered, in any order; do not include an overall/union box. 2D = [west, south, east, north] = [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]; 3D = [west, south, min_z, east, north, max_z]. WGS84 (EPSG:4326); elevation in metres.

crs.description: Coordinate reference system of the data: an authority code such as EPSG:4326 or ESRI:54052, or an OGC CRS URI. A PROJ or WKT string only when no code exists.

geography.description: Countries and regions: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (PER), UN M49 regions (m49:419) or global (vocab/geography.json).

processing_steps.description: ids of processing[] steps that produced this asset.

access_method.description: How the data is reached through this entry: download, service, landing_page or request.

kind.description: Kind of data in this entry (raster, vector, tabular, document, mixed, other).

access.description: Access of this entry, when it differs from the record's.

dataAsset.$comment: A public resource needs a location (minimum level); data on request may have none.

bboxCoords.description: A single bounding box: 2D [west, south, east, north], or 3D [west, south, min_z, east, north, max_z]. WGS84 (EPSG:4326); elevation in metres.

date.description: Date or date-time. Use YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-06-23) or an RFC 3339 date-time (e.g. 2026-06-23T00:00:00Z).

coverageDate.description: ISO 8601 date/time; the precision states the granularity - year (2020), month (2020-06), day (2020-06-23), or an instant (2020-06-23T00:00:00Z). As an end, it is inclusive through the end of that period (end: 2010 means through 2010-12-31).

id.description: Permanent identifier, unique in its catalogue; never reused or changed. MOSAIC uses MFL-YYYY-NNN; CDH-style lowercase ids are also valid.
id of the Hub record linked. Must resolve to exactly one catalog record.

rel.description: Link relation type, e.g. cite-as or describedby.

url.description: URL of a resource outside the Hub.

locations.description: Where the data is: a file, a store or directory, a service endpoint, or (marked with access_method) a landing page or the page where it is requested. The first is canonical.

title.description: Optional access label, e.g. HTTPS or S3.

url.description: Absolute URL. In additional_assets[] and a cdh-inventory file_index[] it may instead be a path relative to the record file.

fileSize.description: File size: whole bytes (31100000) or a number and unit (31.1 MB). Units are B, KB, MB, GB, TB, PB, in powers of 1000 (1 KB = 1000 bytes), rounded up to whole bytes.

mediaType.description: Media type (IANA), optionally with format parameters such as profile or version.

dataType.description: Storage type of a column, band, or array. Numeric names follow STAC raster:data_type; text-column names follow Frictionless Table Schema; decimal and binary are CDH additions for binary stores. integer and number are for text formats (CSV, fixed-width, JSON) where width and signedness are not stored. array is a column whose cells hold a list of values; say the element type in description. other is for maps, structs, and nested lists.

categories.description: Coded values, each with a label and optional description.

value.description: The coded value as stored in the data.

label.description: Short human-readable name of the category.

code.description: Software or code that produced this step's output. Omit when none is published.

url.description: Link to the production code or repository.

version.description: Version, tag, or commit of the code.

derived_from.description: Upstream sources this step derived from - the data (e.g. a Zenodo/Dataverse landing page), not code. Each entry has an id (a Hub record) or a url (anything else), not both.

id.description: id of the Hub record used. Must resolve to exactly one catalog record.

url.description: URL of a source outside the Hub.

version.description: Version label of the source release that was used, as the source publishes it.

id.description: Step identifier; one step must use id: source for the original generation.

orcid.description: ORCID iD of the person, as its https://orcid.org/ URL.

ror.description: ROR id of the organization, as its https://ror.org/ URL.

author.description: A citation author: either a person or an organization.

family.description: Family name(s). A person with a single name uses this field alone.

organization.description: Full name of an organization credited as an author.
examples: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

title.description: Cite-as title; may differ from the record's top-level title.

authors.description: Authors in citation order. A person gives family (and usually given); an organization gives organization.

date.description: Publication date or year, e.g. 2024 or 2024-07-15.

publisher.description: Publisher or venue: the data publisher/repository for datasets, or the journal for articles.

text.description: Citation as the source gives it, when it is not structured.

bbox.description: Spatial extent. A single bounding box, or a list of boxes for disjoint coverage - each box is a real area covered, in any order; do not include an overall/union box. 2D = [west, south, east, north] = [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]; 3D = [west, south, min_z, east, north, max_z]. WGS84 (EPSG:4326); elevation in metres.

crs.description: Coordinate reference system of the data: an authority code such as EPSG:4326 or ESRI:54052, or an OGC CRS URI. A PROJ or WKT string only when no code exists.

geography.description: Countries and regions: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (PER), UN M49 regions (m49:419) or global (vocab/geography.json).

landscapes.description: MFL living landscapes the resource covers (vocab/landscapes.json). Required by the MOSAIC profile.

resolution.description: Spatial resolution, for discovery. Grids also describe it in structures (x/y dimensions).

text.description: As the source states it (e.g. district level, 1:50 000).

temporal.description: Coverage extent, precision-aware. Use `date` for a single instant or period (date: 2020 = the year 2020), or `start_date` + `end_date` for a span (end_date: null = open-ended). `date` and `start_date`/`end_date` are mutually exclusive.

date.description: A single instant or period; its precision sets the granularity (year, month, day, or datetime).

end_date.description: End of a span; null for an open-ended series.

update_frequency.description: How often the resource gains new data (vocab/update_frequency.json).

text.description: Period as the source states it, when it has no precise dates.

temporalValues.description: ISO 8601 strings, all at one precision: year, month, day, or an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and offset.

dimensions.description: Cube axes: domain axes (e.g. crop, scenario), a vertical axis (type: z), place-key columns (type: location), and temporal axes (each type: temporal, with a step for regular spacing). The horizontal lat/lon grid is derived from the top-level spatial field and is not declared here.

name.description: Axis name. Must not be "variable": measures are not axes and belong in variables[]; href_template refers to them via the reserved {variable} token.

description.description: What the dimension is; define coded values here, or via reference_system or a sidecar.

type.description: Dimension type. Reserved values change how the dimension is read: `temporal` (an axis of ISO 8601 dates or instants; a structure may declare several), `z` (a vertical axis - depth, height, or pressure level - at most one per structure), `x`, `y`, and `xy` (the horizontal axes in spatial.crs, as STAC datacube spatial x/y and CF axis X/Y: with a numeric step and unit they are a regular grid, xy when both axes share one spacing, else x and y as a pair with their own; without step they are a table's coordinate columns), and `location` (a column identifying a place, such as an admin, basin, station, or H3 cell code - a key, not an axis of space). Any other value names a domain axis after what it varies (crop, scenario, season). `spatial` and `geometry` are rejected, as are lat/lon spellings, so a coordinate axis cannot silently become a domain axis. Lowercase; aliases of `temporal` are rejected too.

reference_system.description: Vocabulary or spatial index the values are coded against; prefer a resolvable URI when one exists (an AGROVOC concept scheme, a boundary set such as https://gadm.org/, https://h3geo.org/).

step.description: Spacing between consecutive values, as in STAC datacube: an ISO 8601 duration (P1Y, P3M, PT6H) on a type: temporal dimension, a number in unit on x, y, or xy. Not the length of the period a value represents. On a temporal axis, required with extent and omitted when irregular. On a horizontal axis, present for a regular grid and absent for a table's coordinate columns.

extent.description: First and last value of a regular axis, in place of listing every value, as in STAC datacube. On a type: temporal dimension, two ISO 8601 strings at one precision (YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, or an RFC 3339 date-time), no coarser than the step, start before end; requires step and excludes values. On x, y, or xy, the native [min, max] of the axis in unit and spatial.crs, optional, for a grid whose edges spatial.bbox does not give exactly, such as a projected CRS.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the values, in UDUNITS-2 (UCUM only for what UDUNITS-2 cannot express). Required on x, y, and xy (degree, m, km) and on z (cm, m, hPa); useful on any numeric domain axis. Not a substitute for reference_system.

data_type.description: Storage type of the dimension's column or coordinate in the data, distinct from type, which is its role. A temporal dimension's values stay ISO 8601 strings here even when the source stores years as integers.

categories.description: The axis values with labels, in place of values. Not allowed on a type: temporal dimension.

values.description: On a temporal dimension, every value is an ISO 8601 date or an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and offset, as a string. A value that labels a window is one date, such as its start; the dimension description gives the window length. A cyclic label axis (DJF/MAM/JJA/SON) is not temporal - name it after what it varies and describe the labels. All values share one precision.

allOf.$comment: Horizontal axes carry their unit and never enumerate coordinates.
x and y come as a pair, and never beside xy.

description.description: Stable definition and reading guidance for the variable.

data_type.description: Data type of the stored values. Numeric names follow STAC raster:data_type; the rest cover table columns. other is for nested types (list, map, struct).

unit.description: Unit of measurement in UDUNITS-2, as CF requires (mm d-1, degC, kg ha-1). UCUM only for what UDUNITS-2 cannot express, such as {head}/km2 or [pH]; never a UCUM spelling of a UDUNITS-2 unit. Required for measurements; omit for text or code columns.

nodata.description: Fill value for missing data, as stored in this variable. A representation that stores the variable with another fill value or type is another structure.

categories.description: Codes the variable can contain and what each means. For long lists, link a sidecar with rel=describedby instead.

foreignKeys.description: Keys from this table to other catalogued datasets, after Frictionless Table Schema foreignKeys. Each entry pairs this record's key columns with the referenced dataset's columns, positionally.

fields.description: Key columns in this record; each must be a dimensions[]/variables[] name of the same structure.

resource.description: The dataset referenced (e.g. a boundary/station record): its catalog record id, which must resolve to exactly one catalog record, or an absolute URI for a dataset outside the catalog.

asset.description: The data[].name of the referenced dataset's file that holds reference.fields. Required when that dataset has more than one data[] entry.

fields.description: Matching columns in the referenced dataset, paired positionally with fields (same length).

hrefTemplate.$comment: Braces balance; a token is {name} or {name:format}, and a format holds at least one directive and no other %.

description: Structure of a MOSAIC metadata record. Built on the CGIAR Climate Data Hub core schema v0.5.0 (MIT): the same field names and shapes, plus what MOSAIC needs (themes, landscapes, access method, kinds of data, resolution, licence text, inferred fields). A record that breaks this schema is INVALID. Completeness is checked separately by levels/minimum.schema.json and levels/recommended.schema.json; the MOSAIC profile adds what MOSAIC's own records carry. Only properties defined here or in a declared extension are allowed.

schema_version.description: Version of the MOSAIC standard this record follows (e.g. 0.2.0). Written by the build.

description.description: Canonical human- and AI-readable summary of the resource.

note.description: Caveats, warnings, or interpretation-critical remarks not captured in description.

resource_type.description: Kind of resource the record describes (vocab/resource_type.json).

version.description: Version label of this release of the resource. The source's own label when it has one; otherwise a counter from 1. Letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens only, since it becomes part of a superseded release's id. Not compared or sorted - order comes from previous_version.

previous_version.description: version of the predecessor record (same id), when this supersedes an earlier release.

deprecated.description: true when a newer release (same id) supersedes this record.

parent.description: id of the parent record, when this record is a child representation of it. Omit on top-level records. Must resolve to exactly one catalog record, must not equal this record's id, and must not create a parent cycle.

series.description: Program, initiative, or product brand the resource was published under (e.g. Africa Agriculture Adaptation Atlas, MapSPAM, ACASA). Members may span domains, resolutions, and resource types. Not for grouping representations or releases of a single resource. `name` is the grouping key - use the same spelling on every record in the series; `url` is the series landing page.

language.description: Languages of the content, ISO 639-1 codes (en, es, fr).

themes.description: MOSAIC themes (vocab/themes.json); the first one is the primary theme. CDH domains map to these.

keywords.description: Free-text search terms. Each item is either a plain string, or an object linking the term to an external vocabulary/ontology (e.g., AGROVOC, GEMET).

scheme.description: Resolvable URI of the controlled vocabulary or ontology this term comes from. CDH vocab schemes (.../cdh-metadata-standard/vocab/) belong to cdh.domain / commodities - link an external vocabulary instead.

uri.description: Resolvable URI of the specific concept within `scheme`.

commodities.description: Agricultural commodities the resource describes (crops, livestock), as ids of the CDH commodity vocabulary (e.g. maize, cattle).

usage.description: Use guidance: what the resource was produced for, and what to avoid. Omit when there is nothing to say.

intended_uses.description: Uses the resource was produced for (illustrative, never exhaustive).

not_recommended_for.description: Uses to avoid, each with a reason and an optional alternative.

license.description: Licence of the data as an SPDX expression (CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0 OR CC0-1.0). Without an SPDX code: LicenseRef-<name>, with its text in license_text and, when it exists, a link in additional_links (rel: license).

license_text.description: Text of the licence or terms when there is no SPDX code.

access.description: Access to the data: public, restricted (on request or with an account) or non-public (catalogued, not available outside the holders). DCAT / EU access-rights aligned.

access_note.description: Human-readable access conditions or instructions. Required when access is restricted or non-public; maps to schema.org conditionsOfAccess.

attribution.description: Credit line reusers should reproduce: wording a license or upstream source requires, or the credit the producer asks for. One short statement; do not restate citation. Maps to schema.org creditText.
examples: Contains modified Copernicus Emergency Management Service information [year]

contact.description: People or organizations responsible for the resource. At least one should hold the licensor role.

related_publications.description: Related works such as papers or reports.

additional_links.description: Related links: citation targets, services, or related resources. Each entry has an id (a Hub record) or a url (anything else), not both.

data.description: Data assets for the resource; at least one entry.

additional_assets.description: Sidecar or auxiliary assets, e.g. metadata files or thumbnails.

structures.description: The data dictionary, one structure per layout, after Frictionless Data Package resources: each structure is a self-contained set of dimensions, variables, and foreign keys. A record with one layout has one structure. Names are unique within a structure and may repeat across structures, so two tables can each have a column named value. Every data[] entry names the structures it holds.

name.description: Structure name, unique within structures[]; data[].structures refers to it.

dimensions.description: The dimensions every variable in this structure has. Omit it when the variables vary only over the horizontal grid.

foreign_keys.description: Keys from this structure's columns to other catalogued datasets.

geometry_column.description: Name of the geometry column, for a table with embedded geometries. A geometry column is not a variable.

processing.description: Ordered processing/provenance steps; at least one must have id: source.

derived.description: Record fields filled by a tool that read the data (e.g. spatial.bbox), not by a person.

created.description: Date the record was created (not the data). Written by the build from git when missing.

updated.description: Date the record was last updated (not the data). Written by the build from git when missing.

source_updated.description: When the source last updated the data (not the record).

extensions.description: Extensions this record uses, as name@version (e.g. climate@0.2.0). Only for very particular cases; the core covers everything else.

allOf.$comment: With two or more structures, every data[] entry names the structures it holds. With one, an asset without the field holds it.
{variable} expands over variable names. data[].structures already guarantees them when structures exist; this only rejects a template in a record with no structures at all.
